note: Curated New England solar / net-metering / REC market / regulatory updates for array operators. Each item is tagged with its state (or "region" for New England-wide, "rec" for REC-market-wide); the page filters to the reader's state. Refreshed by a research agent; verify against the linked source before relying on any figure.

items.title: Eversource CT rate case: ~$451M distribution ask (~11%), ~18% all-in with storm costs
items.summary: Eversource's PURA filing seeks roughly $451 million in new distribution revenue — about an 11% residential increase — which rises to a headline ~$727 million (~18%) ask once about $1 billion of 2018–2023 storm-recovery costs are layered in. New rates would take effect July 1, 2027; Attorney General William Tong called the request a 'tone-deaf insult.'

items.title: Rhode Island Energy rate case (Docket 25-45-GE) enters post-hearing briefing
items.summary: After June evidentiary and public-comment hearings in Warwick, the PUC issued a Post-Hearing Guidance Memo on July 16, 2026 and parties filed burden-of-proof briefs. The filing seeks a first-year base-distribution increase of roughly $65.9M electric and $114.7M gas; a decision is expected ahead of the ~September 2026 effective date.

items.title: PURA closes NextEra/Broad Brook solar-fire probe, clears Eversource
items.summary: PURA unanimously adopted a final decision closing its investigation of a March 2025 equipment failure and brush fire at a NextEra-affiliated solar facility in Broad Brook, clearing Eversource and ordering a power-quality review of the NextEra site.

items.title: Rooftop solar eased New England's grid through the late-June/July heat wave
items.summary: During the region's late-June–early-July heat wave, behind-the-meter solar across the six states produced roughly 3,594 MW at the hottest hours — more than the Millstone and Seabrook nuclear plants combined — and at times met about 25% of demand. An Acadia Center analysis found distributed solar saved New England customers at least $130 million in wholesale energy costs between June 28 and July 4; the July 1 peak hit 23,729 MW.
items.source: Maine Public / New England News Collaborative

items.title: NH Gov. Ayotte signs SB 538 extending net metering for queued municipal solar
items.summary: SB 538 supports municipal solar projects up to 5 MW and guarantees the current net-metering credit for 20 years for cities, towns, school districts and counties whose projects were already in the interconnection queue. It was signed July 10, 2026.

items.title: NH enacts HB 1718 creating net-metering credits for solar-charged batteries
items.summary: Gov. Kelly Ayotte signed HB 1718 on July 10, 2026 (Chapter 309), directing the Department of Energy and PUC to build a framework compensating customers for electricity exported to the grid from batteries charged by renewable generators, clarifying that storage can pair with net-metered solar without affecting system-size limits.

items.title: New Hampshire joins states with plug-in ('balcony') solar law under SB 540
items.summary: SB 540, effective July 27, 2026, legalizes portable plug-in solar devices capped at 1,200 watts AC that plug into a standard outlet without permits or a formal interconnection agreement, targeting renters and apartment dwellers while requiring UL-type safety certification.

items.title: CMP temporary distribution rates take effect July 1 (~$4/mo decrease) as rate case proceeds
items.summary: Central Maine Power's refundable temporary distribution rates began July 1, 2026, cutting a typical residential bill about $4/month with no distribution-charge increase for roughly ten months (through April 2027) while its full one-year rate case is reviewed. The Public Advocate notes expiring storm costs alone would have lowered bills about $11/month.

items.title: RI 2026 session recap: solar 'grid access fee' killed, large-solar credits cut
items.summary: Gov. McKee's proposed grid-access fee on net-metering systems of at least 1 MW was eliminated after pushback from developers, unions, and clean-energy advocates; a working-group deal instead lowers virtual-net-metering compensation for large solar and trims the net-metering program cap from 275 MW toward 175 MW by 2031. The session ended June 11, 2026.

items.title: Maine DOER holds first public webinar on front-of-the-meter DER successor program
items.summary: Maine's Department of Energy Resources held Public Webinar #1 on June 25, 2026, presenting its approach and timeline for a new front-of-the-meter distributed energy resources program to replace community-solar NEB. The proposed successor program must be submitted to the MPUC by the statutory deadline of September 30, 2026.

items.title: Vermont PUC's 2026 net-metering order cuts solar compensation for a 7th straight year
items.summary: In Case 26-0291-INV the Public Utility Commission's May 29, 2026 biennial order reduces net-metering compensation for new systems and raises the small-solar siting charge from 4¢ to 5¢/kWh for systems permitted Aug 1, 2026 through Jul 31, 2028. Over 1,000 Vermonters and more than 50 House members had urged the PUC to reject the cuts.

items.title: Green Mountain Power seeks 7.5% rate increase effective Oct 1 (Case 26-0096-TF)
items.summary: Green Mountain Power filed a tariff (Case 26-0096-TF) for a 7.5% rate increase effective with bills on or after Oct 1, 2026 — the final step of its 2023–2026 Multi-Year Regulation Plan — and the PUC held a public hearing on the request.

items.title: ISO New England says grid ready for summer; 8,000+ MW of behind-the-meter solar
items.summary: ISO-NE forecasts a normal-weather summer peak of 25,228 MW (26,473 MW under above-average heat) against 28,717 MW of available resources, and reports more than 8,000 MW of behind-the-meter solar expected to cut demand by over 1,700 MW at the peak hour, pushing the daily peak to 5–6 p.m.

items.title: Massachusetts DPU approves DOER's SMART 3.0 program redesign
items.summary: On May 19, 2026 the Department of Public Utilities approved DOER's redesigned SMART 3.0 program (225 CMR 28.00), replacing the declining-block model with annually adjusted incentive rates and capacity blocks. Program Year 2026 carries 600 MW-AC of capacity, and utilities estimate roughly $4.5 billion in ratepayer cost over 20 years for 2025–2026 projects.

items.title: MA Class I RECs trend toward the $40 ACP as MassCEC auctions 2025-vintage certificates
items.summary: MassCEC's May 14, 2026 REC auction offered 4,629 Vintage 2025 MA Class I RECs and 67 Solar Carve-Out II RECs; Evolution Markets said Class I 2025 REC pricing has been trending toward the $40/MWh Alternative Compliance Payment in a supply-constrained market ahead of the 2025 compliance deadline.

items.title: MA DPU opens net-metering investigation — Docket 25-200
items.summary: The DPU opened Docket 25-200 to examine electric delivery rate design and whether to reduce the value of net-metering credits. Technical sessions ran in spring 2026 with comments due April 30; no changes have been ordered and existing systems are expected to be grandfathered.
